summary: Publish the worker status when something changed, and the tick count only every fifth turn

coordination.notes: The comparison lives in aiIngest.ts for the reason A2 established - anything exported from aiWorkerHost.ts cannot be called by a suite - and publishStatus in the host calls it. The plan's verify is a temporary console.count in the panel; that instrument was replaced by a stronger one rather than skipped, because a render count needs the Settings sheet open and only proves a render happened, while subscribing to the store from devtools counts publications directly. Both halves are checked: the browser run measures how often it publishes with nothing happening, and the suite checks that every field except ticks is compared, driven off the status object's own keys so a field added later is covered without anybody remembering.

checks: in the running app on a freshly started dev server, nothing happening, Settings closed: 10 ticks elapsed and exactly 2 publications - one per fifth turn instead of ten
the same run confirmed the served module was the edited one by fetching it and grepping for TICKS_PER_IDLE_PUBLISH before measuring

decisive lines: 'OK a different tick count alone is not a change - it moves every second by design', 'OK every field of the status except ticks has a changed value to test with  all covered', and one 'a change to X is a change' per field
sabotage - drop journalPending from the comparison: 'FAIL a change to journalPending is a change  3', 69 checked 1 failed, exit 1; restored and md5sum 75c64976754d9315b6eab7a0d4864c44 matched
node tools/run-tests.mjs (DRC_TEST_PORT=7971): all passed, 101 suites, 3094 checks

an earlier measurement on the long-running dev server read 0 ticks and 0 publications. That was the instrument, not the code: the page was holding a broken mid-edit HMR state whose console still carried 'runWorkerOnce is not defined' from an older build. A restarted server on a clean port gave the numbers above.
